note: Source of the ChatGPT plugin package (the ZIP OpenAI's dashboard takes). `pnpm chatgpt-plugin` builds it into .tmp/; `pnpm chatgpt-plugin --check` validates it. `tools` mirrors packages/mcp/src/annotations.ts and apps/api/src/chatgpt-plugin.test.ts keeps the two in step. The test cases run against the reviewer workspace that `pnpm db:seed-reviewer` fills (packages/core/src/reviewer-seed.ts); the dashboard takes exactly 5 of them and exactly 3 negative ones. No credentials go in this file: the reviewer login is entered in the dashboard.

app_info.subtitle: Find leads, send cold email
app_info.description:
Meerko is an open-source outbound engine that ChatGPT runs for you. Tell ChatGPT who you sell to and it uses Meerko to find the right companies and people, find and verify their work emails, and write a short email sequence. Meerko sends it from your own Gmail, Google Workspace, Outlook or any IMAP/SMTP mailbox, inside a send window and daily limits that keep your domain healthy, and stops writing to anyone who replies.

Replies come back to ChatGPT: Meerko handles bounces, unsubscribe requests and out-of-office replies on its own, and ChatGPT sorts the rest (interested, question, not now) and drafts an answer for each one. Each draft waits for your approval before it goes.

What you can ask:
- "Find 25 heads of growth at Series A fintechs in the US and get their emails."
- "Write a three-step sequence for them and show me the first email for each person."
- "Who replied this week? Draft answers to the interested ones."
- "How is my sequence doing?"

You need a Meerko account, which you create when you connect, and a mailbox connected in Meerko to send from. The code is AGPL-3.0, so you can also run the whole thing yourself.

justifications.read_only_justification: Returns the workspace the connection acts on, the user's other workspaces, the credit balance, the sending mode and the ideal customer profile, changing nothing. It returns no plan, price or link to buy.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only the user's own Meerko account.
justifications.destructive_justification: Read-only: it deletes, overwrites and sends nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Switches which of the user's workspaces this connection acts on, creates a new empty workspace for another brand, or renames one.
justifications.open_world_justification: Changes a setting on the user's own Meerko connection, or a workspace private to the user's Meerko account, and nothing outside it.
justifications.destructive_justification: Switching only moves a pointer between the user's workspaces and switching back restores it; creating only adds an empty workspace; renaming changes a label that can be changed back. No lead, sequence or email is removed or sent.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists the workspace's lead tables with their columns and row counts, and the lead counts per pipeline stage, changing nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only the user's own Meerko workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: Read-only: it deletes, overwrites and sends nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates a lead table, renames one, or adds a column to one (or saves a new instruction for an existing AI column).
justifications.open_world_justification: Changes only tables in the user's Meerko workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: Adding a column that already exists with a new prompt overwrites that AI column's instruction, and the previous instruction is not kept. Creating and renaming remove nothing, and rows' values are left as they are.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads rows from a table with their pipeline stage and ICP fit, one lead in full with its sequences and emails, or the rows whose AI column is still empty with the instruction for each, changing nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only the user's own Meerko workspace. Meerko does not run an AI column's instruction or call any model.
justifications.destructive_justification: Read-only: it deletes, overwrites and sends nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Inserts new rows into a table, creating columns for keys it has not seen.
justifications.open_world_justification: The rows are stored in the user's own Meerko workspace and sent nowhere else.
justifications.destructive_justification: Only adds rows; existing rows are not changed or removed.

justifications.read_only_justification: Writes values into existing rows of a table, moves leads to a pipeline stage, or saves a manual adjustment of -30 to 30, with a note, on rows' ICP fit scores.
justifications.open_world_justification: Changes only rows in the user's own Meerko workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: A value written to a cell that already had one overwrites it, and an ICP adjustment replaces the adjustment and note saved on the row before; the earlier ones are not kept.

justifications.read_only_justification: Deletes a table with its rows and its paused or draft sequences, leads (rows) from a table, a sequence with its steps and enrollments, or a pending reply draft.
justifications.open_world_justification: Deletes only from the user's own Meerko workspace; nothing is sent.
justifications.destructive_justification: What it deletes is deleted permanently and cannot be restored.

justifications.read_only_justification: Saves the people or companies it finds as new rows in a table and spends one credit per result. With count_only it only returns a number.
justifications.open_world_justification: Searches a third-party database of business contacts and companies, which is outside the user's Meerko account.
justifications.destructive_justification: Only adds rows; nothing existing is changed or removed, and nobody is contacted.

justifications.read_only_justification: Saves the workspace's ideal customer profile and rescores every lead against it.
justifications.open_world_justification: Changes only a setting and the derived fit scores inside the user's Meerko workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: Replaces the whole saved profile: a field left out is cleared, and the previous profile is not kept. Every lead's fit score is then overwritten with one computed from the new profile. Leads, their data and their emails are kept.

justifications.read_only_justification: Fetches a company's public home page and returns its title, description, headings and visible text. Nothing is saved or changed.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads any public website the user names, which is outside the user's Meerko account. Private and internal addresses are refused.
justifications.destructive_justification: Read-only: it deletes, overwrites and sends nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Writes the email, its certainty and verification result (or a phone number) into rows, and spends credits for each one found.
justifications.open_world_justification: Looks contact details up with third-party data providers, which are outside the user's Meerko account. No email is sent to the person.
justifications.destructive_justification: Spends the user's credits for each email, verification or phone number found, and spent credits are not returned. With overwrite, a row that already has a result is run again and its earlier result is replaced; without it, only rows with no result are filled.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists the connected sending mailboxes with their limits, ramp and status, and with check_domains looks up the SPF, DKIM and DMARC records of the domains they send from, changing nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: With check_domains it queries public DNS, which is outside the user's Meerko account. Without it, it reads only the user's own Meerko workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: Read-only: it deletes, overwrites and sends nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Starts connecting a mailbox to the workspace (it returns a sign-in link, or the steps for an app password, that the user completes in the browser), or changes a connected mailbox's daily send limit, sender name or ramp, or lifts a hold Meerko put on it.
justifications.open_world_justification: Connecting only hands the user a link to Meerko's connect page or to Google's or Microsoft's own sign-in; the tool contacts no mailbox and no password passes through the chat. Updating changes only sending settings stored in the user's Meerko workspace and sends no email.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is connected until the user finishes the sign-in themselves, and mailbox settings can be set back at any time; no mailbox, lead or email is removed.

justifications.read_only_justification: Sends one test email from a connected mailbox to the address given.
justifications.open_world_justification: A real email leaves the user's mailbox for an inbox outside Meerko.
justifications.destructive_justification: A sent email cannot be taken back.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists the workspace's sequences, or returns one sequence's stats and mailbox pool usage, renders its steps for one row as they would be sent, or lists the sequence emails waiting for the user's approval. Nothing is saved or sent.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only the user's own Meerko workspace; nothing is sent.
justifications.destructive_justification: Read-only: it deletes, overwrites and sends nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates an email sequence in draft status for a table, edits a sequence's name, mailbox pool, send window or steps, or pauses it.
justifications.open_world_justification: Changes only sequences stored in the user's Meerko workspace; it sends no email itself, and pausing stops email rather than sending it.
justifications.destructive_justification: New steps replace all the existing ones and the previous text is not kept; removing a mailbox from the pool stops the leads that were mid-thread on it. Creating only adds a draft, and pausing keeps every step and enrollment.

justifications.read_only_justification: Adds rows from the sequence's table to the sequence as enrollments.
justifications.open_world_justification: In a sequence that is already running, the enrolled people are emailed from the user's mailbox, at inboxes outside Meerko. In a draft or paused sequence nothing is sent until it is started.
justifications.destructive_justification: Enrolling into a running sequence leads to real emails, which cannot be taken back once sent. By default each email still waits for the user's approval.

justifications.read_only_justification: Sets a sequence to active, so its emails start going out on schedule.
justifications.open_world_justification: Real emails go from the user's mailbox to the enrolled people's inboxes, outside Meerko.
justifications.destructive_justification: Emails that have been sent cannot be taken back; pausing only stops the ones not yet sent.

justifications.read_only_justification: Marks leads' next sequence email as approved, which releases it to be sent when due, or sends a reply draft as a reply in its email thread.
justifications.open_world_justification: The approved emails go from the user's mailbox to people's inboxes outside Meerko.
justifications.destructive_justification: Once an approved email or reply has been sent it cannot be taken back.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists replies to the user's sequences with the thread and the lead's row, or the reply drafts waiting for the user, changing nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads replies and drafts Meerko has already stored in the user's workspace; the tool does not contact the mailbox provider.
justifications.destructive_justification: Read-only: it deletes, overwrites and sends nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Saves an intent on a reply (interested, question, not now and so on) and can mark it handled.
justifications.open_world_justification: Changes only a label in the user's Meerko workspace; the person who replied sees nothing.
justifications.destructive_justification: Sets a label that can be set again; the reply itself is kept.

justifications.read_only_justification: Saves a draft answer to a reply for the user to review, or sends it at once in a workspace the user has set to send reply drafts automatically.
justifications.open_world_justification: In a workspace the user has switched to automatic sending, the draft is emailed at once to the person who replied, outside Meerko. By default it is only stored, and sending is the separate approve_emails tool.
justifications.destructive_justification: With automatic sending on, the draft goes out as a real email, which cannot be taken back. Drafting again for the same reply also replaces the pending draft's text.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates or updates contacts in the CRM the user connected (HubSpot or Attio) from the table's leads.
justifications.open_world_justification: Writes to a third-party CRM, which is outside Meerko, with the access the user granted in the dashboard.
justifications.destructive_justification: Creates contacts in the user's HubSpot or Attio (in Attio also a company record when none has the lead's domain), and for a contact it matches by email it overwrites the fields the lead has a value for (name, job title, company, and in HubSpot the Lead status); the CRM's earlier values are not kept by Meerko, and Meerko cannot undo the push. A lead's empty fields overwrite nothing, no contact is deleted and no message is sent.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates, edits, pauses, resumes and deletes the user's Autopilot routines (a saved brief plus when it runs); the list and get actions only read them.
justifications.open_world_justification: The run_now action makes Meerko call a service outside the user's Meerko account: the Claude routine or the webhook URL the user connected in the dashboard, which starts the user's own AI. The other actions only change routine records in the user's workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: The delete action removes a routine for good, and update overwrites its name, brief and schedule.

justifications.read_only_justification: Records that a routine run has started, so it writes a run record, and returns the routine's brief.
justifications.open_world_justification: Writes only to the user's own Meerko workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: Adds a run record and changes nothing that already exists.

test_cases.description: Read the lead tables and the leads in one of them.
test_cases.user_prompt: Which lead tables do I have in Meerko? Show me the people in the demo one.
test_cases.expected_output: Names the table "Demo leads: B2B SaaS founders" with 8 rows, then lists its eight leads with name, title and company (for example Maya Okafor, Founder & CEO at Ledgerline, and Jonas Berg, VP Sales at Fjordly) and each one's pipeline stage. Nothing is changed.

test_cases.description: Preview a sequence email as a lead would receive it, without sending anything.
test_cases.user_prompt: Show me my Meerko sequences and how the first email reads for one of the leads.
test_cases.expected_output: Shows one sequence, "Founders: agent-run outbound", paused, with 6 leads enrolled. Then shows its three steps rendered for one lead: the first has a subject like "Ledgerline and outbound, Maya" and a body that opens with the lead's first name, and the two follow-ups come 3 and 4 days later. No email is sent.

test_cases.description: Write a draft answer to an interested reply and leave it for review.
test_cases.user_prompt: Priya replied that she is interested. Draft a short answer in Meerko proposing Thursday at 3pm, and don't send it yet.
test_cases.expected_output: Finds the reply from Priya Nair at Quaystack ("Yes, let's talk. Thursday afternoon works for me."), saves a short draft that proposes Thursday at 3pm, shows its text and says it is waiting for approval. Nothing is sent.

test_cases.description: Report the pipeline and how the sequence is doing.
test_cases.user_prompt: How is my outbound going in Meerko? Give me the pipeline and the numbers for my sequence.
test_cases.expected_output: Reports the pipeline for the demo workspace: 2 new, 3 contacted and 3 replied leads, none in meeting, won or lost. For the sequence "Founders: agent-run outbound" it reports 6 leads enrolled, 6 emails sent and 3 replies, and that the sequence is paused.

test_cases.description: Count matching leads in the lead database without saving them or spending credits.
test_cases.user_prompt: With Meerko, how many CTOs at fintech companies in Spain could I reach? Just count them, don't save anything.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns the number of people matching a CTO title at financial-services companies in Spain. It says the count is free, and no rows are saved and no credits are spent.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not trigger for the user's general inbox. Meerko reads only replies to the sequences it sent, not the rest of a mailbox.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Summarise the unread emails that arrived in my inbox this morning.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Meerko should not be invoked. If asked about it, ChatGPT explains that Meerko only shows replies to its own sequences.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not trigger for social media. Meerko sends email and has no tool that posts or sends messages on social networks.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Write a LinkedIn post announcing our seed round and publish it on my profile.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Meerko should not be invoked, because it cannot post to LinkedIn or any social network.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not trigger for general knowledge about sales or email with nothing to look up or do in the user's workspace.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: What is a good reply rate for B2B cold email, and what is the difference between SPF and DKIM?
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Meerko should not be invoked: this is a general question, answered from ChatGPT's own knowledge.

plugin.note: Fields only the plugin package needs; the rest of the package is derived from app_info and the test cases above. `name` is the package id of a first upload: once the dashboard has a listing, the id it assigned may have to go here instead, or the upload is refused. `developerName` is replaced by the verified identity on the dashboard. `demoRecordingURL` stays null until the walkthrough video exists; the package builds without it but cannot be submitted.
